history.summary: Large 1,378 sqft 3BR by reputable Sim Lian at Bedok Reservoir, priced at PSF 1379 — a strong ~8% discount to the project's URA median of 1502 — with 7.4%/yr resale appreciation on a deep 178-txn base and a $1.9M quantum in the sweet spot. Reservoir-facing stacks avoid road noise; this is a well-priced, liquid Buy.
history.rating_rationale: PSF 1379 vs URA median 1502 is a clean ~8% discount on a genuinely large 1,378 sqft 3BR — good value per square foot. 7.4%/yr resale CAGR on 178 transactions is reliable, 696 units and a $1.9M quantum (centre of the deep buyer band) support easy exit, and Sim Lian is a solid builder. Bedok Reservoir lifestyle draw and proximity to Tampines Regional Centre underpin demand. The main caveat is unit-specific: quarry/road-facing stacks suffer traffic noise, so the reservoir-facing stacks are the ones to target. No MRT directly at the door is the structural weak point but the discount and size compensate.

history.summary: Sim Lian D18 development (696 units) at a low $1399 PSF, ~7% below the $1502 median, with a 7.36% CAGR over a deep 178 transactions and a low $1.1M quantum. The persistent drawback is connectivity — no MRT within walking distance and a busy 4-lane road outside — which keeps it a balanced Neutral despite genuine value on price.
history.rating_rationale: Real positives: below-median PSF ($1399 vs $1502), the deepest data confidence in the batch (178 txns, 7.36% CAGR), large 696-unit liquidity, and a low $1.1M quantum that widens the buyer pool. But the blank MRT field and a busy 4-lane arterial road outside are structural negatives for an investment hold — the transit-reliant tenant majority is deflected and resale appeal is capped. Design gripes (units facing each other, no direct reservoir access despite the name) further dull the premium-buyer case. Value on price, but the connectivity gap balances it to Neutral.

history.summary: Genuinely under-priced 2BR in an OCR (D18) lakeside project with a deep transaction base and a long lease runway.
history.rating_rationale: Asking 1399 psf sits clearly below the project's last-12-month average of ~1479 psf (recent range 1174-1655 psf), so the algo's -4.7% age-adjusted and -9.1% cohort discounts are corroborated by real recent resale evidence (psf_cohort_txns 7 is thin but the broader 178-txn project base is deep). It is OCR, the region with the strongest realized forward returns (~+4.0%) under the v3.4 priors, with ~88 years of lease left (2014 completion, 99yr from 2010) and a sub-$1.1m quantum that keeps the 2BR liquid. Trailing 7.36% CAGR (178 txns) is credible but treated as story, not a forward guarantee. The discount-to-comps plus region tailwind justify a Buy; medium confidence because there is no specific dated catalyst and the bargain rests on a modest 5% gap.
red_flags: Thin same-size cohort (psf_cohort_txns 7) means the 9.1% cohort discount rests on few direct comps
Busy 4-lane road frontage and ~15-min walk to nearest supermarket / no direct reservoir access (per reviews) cap livability and rental pull
No dated MRT or zoning catalyst to drive re-rating
catalysts: Bedok Reservoir / Tampines Quarry waterfront amenity and ongoing Tampines North precinct build-out
OCR region tailwind (~+4.0% realized forward vs CCR ~+0.7%)

history.summary: This is not a 3-bedder. The 926 sqft unit at Waterview (91 Tampines Ave 1, Sim Lian, TOP Jan 2014, 696 units, 99yrs from 16 Jun 2010 so ~83 left) is a 2-BEDROOM + STUDY that the agent has relabelled as a 3BR: Sim Lian's own unit mix lists 926 sqft under 2-bedroom/2+study, URA-derived transaction data buckets Waterview 2-bed at 786-980 sqft and 3-bed at 1,109-1,572 sqft, and URA rental contracts file 926 sqft units as 2-bedroom. Real 3BRs here start at 1,109 sqft and cost $450-650k more. On price the ask is honest -- $1,402 psf against a last-12-month median of $1,464 psf / $1,355,000 for this exact 925.7 sqft layout (35 URA prints, 12 in 24 months), i.e. ~4% cheap and inside the genuine p10-p50 zone, not an artifact. But the forward case does not survive contact with the data: Waterview's resale median has been flat for 18 months and all of D18 with it, the true yield is 3.7% (not the 4.25% shown, which used the wrong bed bucket), and roughly 4,000 new private units land across Tampines/Pasir Ris inside a 5-7 year hold -- including ~1,145 sited directly on Tampines West MRT, the station Waterview is 1.4km from. Fair price, wrong product, no edge.
history.rating_rationale:
AVOID -- but not because the price is wrong. The ask is fair. It fails on product and on forward return.

1. IT IS NOT A 3BR, AND THAT IS THE BRIEF. The owner's screen is 3BR, OCR, up to ~$1.8M. This 926 sqft unit is a 2-bedroom + study, verified three independent ways: Sim Lian's own project page lists the mix as 2-bedroom / 2+study / 3-bedroom / 3+study / 4-bedroom / penthouse and places 926 sqft in the 2-bed tier; URA-derived transaction data buckets Waterview 2-bed at 786-980 sqft and 3-bed at 1,109-1,572 sqft; and URA rental contracts file 926 sqft units under '2 bedrooms, 900-1,000 sqft'. Agents market the same 926 sqft interchangeably as '3 Bed 3 Bath' and '3 Bed 2 Bath'. Genuine Waterview 3BRs are 1,109-1,184 sqft and transact at $1.78M-$2.01M -- $450-650k above this. The DB record's `beds: 3` is the agent's label, not URA's classification, so every '3BR' framing in this dossier is inherited from the listing.

2. THE YIELD IN THE DOSSIER IS WRONG, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS. The 4.25% gross rests on $4,600/mo drawn from the URA 3-bedroom bucket -- but URA files this unit as a 2-bedder, and the correct series is the 900-1,000 sqft band, which transacted at $3,500-$4,100/mo through 2026 (Jun-26 prints: $4,100 / $3,700 / $3,500) with the current 926 sqft asking rent at $4,000. At $4,000/mo the true gross yield is 3.70%, not 4.25%, and EdgeProp independently puts Waterview's average yield at 3.4%. Rescored at 2 beds, $4,000 rent and a 3.5%/yr forward rate, score_1000 falls from 788 to 559 and the all-cash 5yr annualized ROI falls from 7.57% to 4.02%.

3. THE 7.36% TRAILING CAGR EXPIRED IN MID-2024. Waterview's resale median PSF: 2024H2 $1,470, 2025H1 $1,499, 2025H2 $1,495, 2026H1 $1,502 -- flat for 18 months. Not project-specific: D18 resale-only medians are $1,488 / $1,500 / $1,469 / $1,496 across the last four half-years on 1,724 prints. This exact 926 sqft layout is actually DOWN, from a 2024H2 median of $1,510 to $1,464. The algo's 788 is built on this dead channel: appreciation contributes +10.08 of MMR, its single largest positive, from a signal the repo's own backtest gives ~zero forward power (marginal +0.03).

4. SUPPLY LANDS ON TOP OF IT, INCLUDING ON ITS OWN STATION. Confirmed Tampines/Pasir Ris pipeline: Pinery Residences (Hoi Hup/Sunway, Tampines St 94, ~585 units, DIRECT connection to Tampines West MRT, $2,100-2,400 psf indicative, preview Q2-Q3 2026); Tampines St 95 GLS (~560 units, also short walk to Tampines West); Parktown Residence (1,193 units, Tampines Ave 11, 87% sold on launch weekend at $2,360 psf, integrated with mall/bus interchange/the future CRL Tampines North station); Tampines St 62 Parcel B EC (Sim Lian, ~700 units); Coastal Cabana EC, Pasir Ris (748 units, 67% sold at $1,734 psf, est. TOP 2029). That is roughly 3,800-4,000 private units, plus Tampines BTO keys around 2028-29 from HDB's 19,600-flat 2026 programme. The ~1,145 units at Pinery and St 95 are the direct threat: they take Waterview's own MRT and do it properly, brand new. Waterview's CRL exposure is nominal -- Tampines North station opens 2030 but sits 2,736m away and its uplift accrues to Parktown.

5. THE CAPITAL CASE DOES NOT CLEAR ABSD. The dossier's ROI assumes SC first property at 0% ABSD (scoring/roi.py line 42). On an investment purchase this carries $259,600 ABSD plus $36,520 BSD -- ~22.8% of price before a dollar of profit. At 3.5%/yr, seven years of growth is +27.2%, which barely covers entry plus ~2% exit costs. roi.py's own note puts the SC-second-property hit at ~19pp on 5yr ROI: a 21.8% five-year total becomes ~3%, or ~0.6%/yr. The return would be rent carry alone, at a net yield near 2%.

6. THE ONE POSITIVE IS SMALLER THAN THE UNCERTAINTY AROUND IT. The ~4% discount is real and verified against the layout's own prints, but the same-layout 24-month floor spread is ~6% ($1,442 for 01-05, $1,472 for 06-10, $1,533 for 11-15) and this unit's floor and facing are UNKNOWN -- floor_level and facing are 0% populated and no Waterview profile exists. The three cheapest prints in the set ($1,361 / $1,367 / $1,404) all came from the 01-05 and 06-10 bands. So the discount may simply be a low floor. Research also confirms the project splits into a quiet reservoir-facing side with no road separation and a quarry-facing side with a major road between -- and which of the 13 blocks (71-95 Tampines Ave 1; this unit is block 91) sits where could not be established from any public site plan.

WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD, FOR THE RECORD: the ask is fair-to-slightly-cheap and verified, not an artifact; exit liquidity is excellent (696 units, 178 URA prints in 5 years, deep buyer pool); 83 years of lease leaves ~76 at a 2033 exit; the $1.298M quantum sits in the most-traded Tampines band; the seller is motivated, having cut $1,500,000 -> $1,350,000 -> $1,298,000 in seven weeks; Sim Lian Construction holds BCA A1 grade and no Waterview-specific defect, MCST or en-bloc issue could be found; and rental demand is real, with Temasek Polytechnic ~200m away and Changi Business Park nearby. As a 2BR+study bought for yield this would be a defensible Neutral -- it out-yields Waterview's true 3BRs (3.7% vs ~2.8%). It is the 3BR-investment-for-resale-profit brief it fails, on both product and forward return.
red_flags: NOT A 3-BEDROOM. 926 sqft at Waterview is a 2-bedroom + study. Sim Lian's own unit mix places it in the 2-bed tier; URA-derived transaction data buckets Waterview 2-bed at 786-980 sqft and 3-bed at 1,109-1,572 sqft; URA rental contracts file 926 sqft units as '2 bedrooms, 900-1,000 sqft'. Agents relabel the study as bedroom 3 and market the same layout inconsistently as '3 Bed 3 Bath' and '3 Bed 2 Bath'. Real Waterview 3BRs are 1,109-1,184 sqft and cost $450-650k more. This fails the owner's 3BR screen outright.

The dossier's 4.25% gross yield is wrong because it drew from the URA 3-bedroom bucket ($4,600/mo). The correct 900-1,000 sqft series transacted at $3,500-$4,100/mo through 2026 with the current 926 sqft asking rent at $4,000, giving a true gross yield of 3.70%; EdgeProp independently puts Waterview's average yield at 3.4%. Net yield falls to roughly 2%.

Price growth has stopped. Waterview resale median PSF 2024H2 $1,470 -> 2025H1 $1,499 -> 2025H2 $1,495 -> 2026H1 $1,502, flat for 18 months, and D18 resale-only medians are flat across four half-years ($1,488 / $1,500 / $1,469 / $1,496 on 1,724 prints). This exact 926 sqft layout is DOWN, from a 2024H2 median of $1,510 to $1,464.

The algo's score_1000 of 788 is trailing-CAGR inflation: appreciation is +10.08 of MMR, its largest positive, from a 2021-2024 CAGR the repo's own backtest gives ~zero forward power. Rescored at 2 beds, $4,000 rent and a 3.5%/yr forward rate, score_1000 falls to 559 and 5yr all-cash annualized ROI falls from 7.57% to 4.02%.

Roughly 3,800-4,000 new private units land in Tampines/Pasir Ris inside a 5-7yr hold: Pinery Residences (~585 units, direct connection to Tampines West MRT, $2,100-2,400 psf, preview Q2-Q3 2026), Tampines St 95 GLS (~560 units, also near Tampines West), Parktown Residence (1,193 units at $2,360 psf), Tampines St 62 Parcel B EC (~700 units), Coastal Cabana EC Pasir Ris (748 units, est. TOP 2029) -- plus Tampines BTO keys ~2028-29. The ~1,145 units at Pinery and St 95 sit directly on Waterview's own MRT station.

Floor and facing UNKNOWN -- floor_level/facing are 0% populated (known broken enricher) and no Waterview profile exists (stack_profile.status = not_researched). The same-layout 24-month floor spread ($1,442 for 01-05, $1,472 for 06-10, $1,533 for 11-15) is ~6%, WIDER than the ~4% discount claimed, and the three cheapest prints in the set all came from the lower bands. The discount may simply be a low floor.

The project splits into a quiet reservoir-facing side (no road separation) and a quarry-facing side with a major road between it and Tampines Quarry. Which of the 13 blocks (71-95 Tampines Ave 1 -- this unit is block 91) faces which could not be established from any public site plan, so noise exposure is unresolved.
The name oversells it: despite adjoining Bedok Reservoir there is NO direct water access -- residents must exit the development, walk along the road and enter via a car park, about 5 minutes.

ABSD is absent from the ROI model, which assumes SC first property at 0%. On an investment purchase this is $259,600 ABSD plus $36,520 BSD, ~22.8% of price. At 3.5%/yr, seven years of growth (+27.2%) barely covers entry plus exit costs; roi.py's own note puts the SC-second-property hit at ~19pp on 5yr ROI, turning a ~21.8% five-year total into ~3%.

No MRT and no catalyst that touches this asset: 1.4km to Tampines West (DTL) -- about a 20-minute walk per an on-site review -- is the largest single MMR negative at -7.13, and the CRL Tampines North station (opening 2030) is 2,736m away with its uplift accruing to Parktown Residence.

REALSCORE and every realsmart profitability metric are NULL for Waterview (cache resolved but empty), so the project-level 'has this ever lost owners money' downside check could not be performed at all.

Ask sits at only the ~17th percentile of the 24-month same-layout print set, near the bottom edge -- consistent with either a motivated seller or a low-floor/road-facing unit, and the data cannot distinguish them.

Lease optics: 99 years ran from 16 Jun 2010 but TOP was Jan 2014, so ~3.6 years were burned before anyone moved in. Balance is ~83 years -- not a problem in this hold window, but the clock is older than the building.

Soft maintenance signals: EdgeProp resident reviews describe management as 'rude' and the 1.2m pool depth as inadequate; a site walkthrough noted ongoing carpark repair works and dirty carpark stairs. No Waterview-specific defect, MCST lawsuit or en-bloc activity was found, but that is absence of evidence, not evidence of absence.
catalysts: Verified value, not an artifact: $1,402 psf against a last-12-month same-layout median of $1,464 psf / $1,355,000, backed by 35 URA prints of this exact 925.7 sqft layout (12 in 24 months). The ask sits inside the rubric's p10-p50 genuine-deal zone -- the sqft and format are real.

Cheap on both relative-value reads: -3.0% vs the age-adjusted D18 median and -15.5% vs new-launch-implied fair PSF. Cheap-vs-district-peers is the strongest forward signal that survives the repo's backtest.

Motivated seller with more room below: ask cut $1,500,000 -> $1,350,000 -> $1,298,000 in seven weeks (a relist chain off listing 500188177). It is now the cheapest active 926 sqft ask in the project, undercutting the $1,350,000 cluster by ~4% and the $1,450,000 ask by ~10%.
Excellent exit liquidity: 696 units, 178 URA prints in five years, 'deep' buyer-pool depth -- and district buyer-pool depth is one of the few signals that survives clustering (std_beta +0.16).
Quantum sits in the most heavily traded Tampines resale band and leaves ~$500k of the owner's ~$1.8M budget unspent.
OCR region -- the best forward-return prior on the full URA panel (realized forward OCR +3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1% and CCR +1.9%).

83 years of lease remaining (99yrs from 16 Jun 2010), still ~76 at a 2033 exit -- clear of the CPF and financing thresholds that impair older leasehold resales. Age 13 also sits in the 5-30yr band where forward returns plateau, so no age penalty stacks on top.

Better carry than the project's real 3BRs: at ~$4,000/mo on $1.298M this yields ~3.7% gross versus ~2.8% for a 1,184 sqft 3BR at ~$1.93M. If the brief were yield rather than resale profit, this is the right unit at Waterview.

Genuine tenant base that does not depend on the MRT: Temasek Polytechnic is ~200m away (a live room-rental market), Springfield Secondary 500m, and Changi Business Park -- DBS Asia Hub, Standard Chartered, IBM -- is close enough that Tampines is cited as one of the most stable rental submarkets in Singapore. Bus stops sit 240-250m away with six routes and roughly a 5-minute ride to Tampines West.

Reservoir-facing stacks are genuinely quiet -- there is no road between the development and Bedok Reservoir on that side, and residents report unblocked water views. If this unit turns out to be on that side and on a high floor, the value case improves materially.

Developer quality is not a concern: Sim Lian Construction holds BCA A1 grade and no Waterview-specific defect, lawsuit or en-bloc issue surfaced in twelve years post-TOP (the well-documented Sim Lian defect complaints attach to Centrale 8 DBSS, a different project).

Honest counterpoint to the MRT objection: Stacked Homes' June-2026 review of Waterview is titled 'This Condo Beat Almost Every Other Tampines Project For 10 Years, And It Wasn't Even Near An MRT' -- the project has historically outperformed its district despite the 1.4km walk, which suggests the transit penalty is at least partly already in the price. Treat this as story rather than forward signal: it is trailing performance, the body of the review is paywalled and unread, and the outperformance stopped in mid-2024 on our own URA data.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment:
Respectable carry, materially below what the dossier shows, and facing a supply wall mid-hold. The dossier's $4,600/mo and 4.25% gross yield are wrong for this unit: that figure comes from the URA 3-bedroom bucket, which pools 926 through 1,184 sqft, while URA itself files 926 sqft Waterview units under '2 bedrooms, 900-1,000 sqft'. The correct series ran $3,500-$4,100/mo through 2026 (June-2026 prints at $4,100 / $3,700 / $3,500; May-2026 at $4,100 / $3,800; April-2026 at $3,950 / $3,600) with the current 926 sqft asking rent at $4,000. That puts true gross yield at 3.70% and net nearer 2%, against EdgeProp's independently published 3.4% project average. The one genuinely favourable comparison is internal: a real 1,184 sqft 3BR here rents at ~$4,500 on a ~$1.93M price for ~2.8% gross, so the compact unit is the better carry per dollar within this project.

Demand itself is real and unusually diversified for a non-MRT project. Temasek Polytechnic sits ~200m away and sustains a live room-rental market; Changi Business Park -- DBS's Asia Hub, Standard Chartered's regional processing centre, IBM -- puts thousands of well-paid finance and tech staff within a short commute, and Tampines is routinely cited as one of the most stable rental submarkets for exactly that reason; Singapore Expo, Changi Airport and Tampines Regional Centre add depth; and six bus routes from stops 240m away reach Tampines West in about five minutes. Waterview recorded 92 URA rental contracts in twelve months, which is a healthy churn for 696 units.

The forward risk is supply, and it is concentrated exactly where it hurts. Coastal Cabana EC (748 units) is estimated for TOP around 2029; Parktown Residence (1,193 units) and the Tampines St 62 EC (~700 units) follow; Pinery Residences (~585 units) and Tampines St 95 (~560 units) will deliver brand-new stock sitting directly on Tampines West MRT. Tampines BTO completions around 2028-29 add to the same pool. A 1.4km-from-MRT 2BR+study competes for tenants against all of it in years 3-5 of the hold. Treat the ~3.7% as decent today, plan for pressure mid-hold, and per the v3.10 panel never read it as appreciation -- gross yield's multivariate forward-price std_beta is -0.16.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment:
The trailing number is real and entirely spent. Waterview's 178 URA prints give a 5-year CAGR of 7.36-8.2%/yr, and this exact 926 sqft layout ran $1,012 psf in 2021H2 to $1,464 over the last twelve months, +44.7%. All of it happened by mid-2024. Project resale median PSF by half-year: 2023H2 $1,350, 2024H1 $1,426, 2024H2 $1,470, then 2025H1 $1,499, 2025H2 $1,495, 2026H1 $1,502 -- eighteen months flat. The plateau is district-wide, not a project story: D18 resale-only medians read $1,488, $1,500, $1,469, $1,496 across the last four half-years on 1,724 prints. The subject's own format has done worse than flat, sliding from a 2024H2 median of $1,510 to $1,464. The dossier's momentum field already reads -1.0, and EdgeProp's published Waterview average of $1,493 psf corroborates the level.

Forward view: I have overridden the 7.36% data rate to 3.5%/yr on resale-to-resale evidence, since the project's and the district's own resale medians have delivered roughly 0%/yr for two years and the repo's priors give trailing CAGR ~zero forward power. 3.5% sits just under the realized forward OCR average of +3.7%/yr: the -3.0% age-adjusted value cushion argues up, while three drags argue down -- the 1.4km MRT deficit (a real backtested signal at std_beta -0.11), this format's demonstrated ~3% underperformance over 24 months, and a competitive set that is about to get much better. Pinery Residences and Tampines St 95 will put ~1,145 brand-new units directly on Tampines West MRT at $2,100-2,400 psf, and Parktown Residence already sold 87% of 1,193 units at $2,360 psf on a site integrated with a mall, bus interchange and the CRL Tampines North station opening in 2030. Waterview's role in that market shifts from 'the affordable Tampines condo' to 'the old one further from the station'.

At 3.5%/yr the unit exits near $1.54M at five years and $1.65M at seven ($1,665 and $1,784 psf). That is not implausible -- $1,784 psf is roughly what better-located D18 stock such as D'Nest, The Palette and Q Bay transacts at today -- but it is not a profit thesis once ~22.8% of entry cost in BSD and ABSD is netted off a +27.2% seven-year gain. The upside case requires the D18 resale plateau to break, which nothing in the current data supports; the downside case is another two flat years with the compact format lagging as ~4,000 new units complete around it.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes:
Partially resolvable, and the unresolved part is decisive. We know the block -- the listing address is 91 Tampines Avenue 1, one of thirteen (71, 73, 75, 77, 79, 81, 83, 85, 87, 89, 91, 93, 95) across a 7.8-acre site at the junction of Tampines Ave 1 and Ave 10, roughly 14-15 storeys with only four units per floor. What we do not know is the floor or the aspect: floor_level and facing are 0% populated by the enricher, stack_profile.status is 'not_researched' (no profiles/waterview.json exists), and no public site plan showing block orientation could be obtained -- SG Floorplans paywalls the floor plates and the one 'premium pool frontage, shielded from road noise and afternoon sun' claim found for a 926 sqft unit is agent marketing, not independent.

That gap is load-bearing because the floor premium exceeds the discount. Same-layout (925.7 sqft) 24-month median PSF runs $1,442 across 01-05 (n=4), $1,472 across 06-10 (n=6) and $1,533 across 11-15 (n=2) -- about a 6% spread against a ~4% discount. A mid-to-high-floor unit at $1,402 is a genuine 5-9% discount; a low-floor unit is at or barely below fair value. The three lowest prints in the set ($1,361, $1,367, $1,404) all came from the 01-05 and 06-10 bands.

Aspect matters at least as much. Research confirms the development has two water outlooks with very different quality: the Bedok Reservoir side has no road between it and the water, so those stacks get unblocked views and no traffic noise, while the Tampines Quarry side is separated by a large road and is the noisy one -- and both prior Waterview evaluations independently flagged the busy Tampines Avenue 1 frontage. It is also confirmed that despite the name there is no direct reservoir access from the development; residents walk out along the road and enter through a car park, about five minutes. One further layout note from a site walkthrough: with four units per floor the main doors face each other directly, which some buyers dislike.

Before any offer, the floor, the block's orientation and the study's configuration (window? full-height enclosure? actual dimensions -- none of which could be verified without a paywalled floor plan) must be confirmed on a viewing. Running /research-development on Waterview would give the join real stack data. Until then the discount is unverified.
